assertions.name: D_trace_difference_classical_floor_is_1_over_8
assertions.source: Richardson extrapolation of tr_M(W_free) - tr_M(W_atom) to q -> 1 along q = exp(eta), eta = 1e-3..1e-6, via tr_m_atom_via_transfer.tr_m_atom_zn, vs the dyadic rational 1/8. The claim under test is that the limit is NONZERO -- i.e. that this observable survives where the Hecke algebra degenerates to C[S_n].

assertions.name: 4He_trace_difference_classical_floor_is_7_over_128
assertions.source: Richardson extrapolation of tr_M(W_free) - tr_M(W_atom) to q -> 1 along q = exp(eta), eta = 1e-3..1e-6, via tr_m_atom_via_transfer.tr_m_atom_zn, vs the dyadic rational 7/128. The claim under test is that the limit is NONZERO -- i.e. that this observable survives where the Hecke algebra degenerates to C[S_n].

assertions.name: trace_difference_deviation_from_the_floor_is_first_order_in_hbar_q
assertions.source: log-log slope of |diff - c0| against hbar_q over eta = 1e-3..1e-6, worst case over the deuteron and 4He (measured D: 1.0017918, 4He: 1.002242). NOT hbar_q^2, which is what E_0_CONVENTIONS['B_q_value_absorbed'] states for this operator class.

assertions.name: delta_net_is_exactly_first_order_with_no_classical_floor
assertions.source: log-log slope of |Delta(net)| = |h(h-2)/2|, h = q - 1/q, against hbar_q over eta = 1e-3..1e-6. h vanishes identically at q = 1, so there is no floor to extrapolate -- this is convention A's operator class and it passes the test the trace difference fails.

assertions.name: plancherel_block_sum_is_second_order_with_no_classical_floor
assertions.source: log-log slope of b_over_a_evaluator.spectral_b_over_a against hbar_q, worst case over D, 4He, 12C (measured D: 2.0002149, 4He: 2.0002152, 12C: 2.0002149). At q = 1 every one-crossing eigenvalue is +-1, so the log-ratio is identically zero and there is no floor.

assertions.name: classical_floor_closed_form_holds_including_at_A_equals_5
assertions.source: worst relative error of the measured floor against c0(A) = 2^-A - 2^(1-2A) over D, T, 3He, 4He, 5Li, 5He. The form is read off A = 2,3,4; A = 5 is a genuine prediction on two isobars that did not enter it. Residuals are Richardson extrapolation error (they grow with A), not discrepancies.

description: Classifies the framework's binding observables by their behaviour as q -> 1. Delta(net) and the Plancherel block sum vanish (hbar_q^1 and hbar_q^2). The signed trace difference does NOT: it has an exact dyadic classical floor (1/8 at the deuteron, 7/128 at 4He) plus an hbar_q^1 deformation, so the E_0 registry's 'carries the hbar_q^2 scaling' is wrong for it and no single E_0 convention pairs with it consistently.

classical_floor_closed_form.depends_on: A only -- NOT the Z/N split. T and 3He agree exactly, so do 5Li and 5He. At q = 1 every one-crossing eigenvalue is +-1 and flavour disappears, so this is the required behaviour.

subtracting_the_floor_costs_the_route_it.reading: The A-route's 4.7% near-hit at the deuteron was 22.46% classical contamination. Removing it -- which the hbar_q bookkeeping requires -- degrades the deuteron to 1.23x short. 4He is ~6x short either way, consistent with the known 4-body alpha residual. Reported because the repair making a number WORSE is the part most likely to be quietly dropped.

classification.registry_operator_class: B_q_value_absorbed, stated as 'carries the hbar_q^2 scaling'
classification.consistent_E0_pairing: NONE -- the floor is hbar_q^0 and the deformation is hbar_q^1, so no single scale pairs with the whole thing

the_two_producers_disagree.note: Same trace difference, two live producers, two conventions, 5.35x apart. The registry rule 'atom level MUST use B' rests on the hbar_q^2 claim this probe refutes, so the rule cannot currently adjudicate. Recorded as an inconsistency to resolve, NOT resolved here -- picking the convention that lands closer to AME would be exactly the fit this lane keeps walking into.

data.what_is_NOT_concluded: That the hbar_q-suppressed route is refuted. Delta(net) and the Plancherel block sum both pass the classical-limit test cleanly, and Delta(net) x convention A still predicts Q_beta to 0.168%. What is refuted is the assumption -- mine, stated last turn without checking -- that the trace difference belongs to that category. It does not, and the registry's hbar_q index for it is wrong by two orders.
data.verdict: tr_M(W_free) - tr_M(W_atom) is NOT a pure deformation observable. It has an exact dyadic classical floor -- 1/8 at the deuteron, 7/128 at 4He, extrapolated to 1e-10 -- plus an hbar_q^1 deformation. At q0 the floor is 22.46% of it for the deuteron and 4.88% for 4He, so that fraction of any binding read off it is present in a framework with no deformation at all. E_0_CONVENTIONS says this operator class 'carries the hbar_q^2 scaling'; measured it carries neither an hbar_q^2 leading term nor a vanishing limit. Since the two parts sit at different orders, no single E_0 convention pairs with it consistently -- and two live producers already disagree by 5.35x about which one to use.
